page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-64-lssd is a compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 248 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB per core. For high-speed local storage, the instance includes six local NVMe SSDs totaling 2078 GB of capacity, while no dedicated GPUs are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities rank in the top 10% and top 25% respectively, supported by advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX_VNNI. Memory performance is highly competitive, with Passmark memory scores and large-block memory read/write bandwidths placing in the top tier and top 25% respectively. Additionally, the platform excels in database operations, software compilation, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds for 7B models reach top-tier thresholds.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy and I/O-intensive workloads due to its dense allocation of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and integrated high-speed NVMe storage. However, the lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for massive-scale deep learning training, and the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio may not suit memory-bound applications requiring massive datasets in-memory. It is highly suited for database hosting, software compilation pipelines, web serving, and medium-scale machine learning inference.
